links.comparator_used: Expert clinician panel scores and independent expert re-scoring panels scoring the same diagnoses
links.outcome: Agreement with expert panel scores, ranking of diagnosing agents, and severe-risk error probability
links.effect: Uncalibrated LLM Jury scores preserved ordinal agreement with the expert panel but were systematically lower. After isotonic regression calibration, scores and rankings showed excellent agreement with the primary expert panels. Severe-risk error probability was lower for the LLM Jury than for the human expert re-score panels. No self-preference bias was found. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Uncalibrated scores were systematically lower, so post hoc calibration was needed. Findings come from LMIC hospital cases and need confirming in other clinical settings.
links.quote: Together, these results provide evidence that a calibrated LLM Jury is a trustworthy and reliable proxy for expert clinician evaluation in medical AI benchmarking.

links.comparator_used: Expert panel review of diagnoses without LLM-based flagging
links.outcome: Identification of diagnoses at high risk of error for targeted expert review, and panel efficiency
links.effect: The LLM Jury combined with LLM diagnoses could identify high-risk diagnoses, enabling targeted expert review and improved panel efficiency. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
links.quote: (iii) the LLM Jury combined with LLM diagnoses can be used to identify diagnoses at high risk of error, enabling targeted expert review and improved panel efficiency;

design_hint: LLM jury scoring with post hoc calibration and targeted expert review
